copy.hero.tagline: Chasing a life of passion and challenge.
copy.hero.intro: I’m Josh—a University of Miami business student drawn to restaurants, consumer brands, and the work behind experiences people come back to. It started with a restaurant job at 15. I’m still following that curiosity.
copy.dimension.food.title: Restaurants & consumer brands
copy.dimension.food.copy: The industry that first got my attention—and the one I keep coming back to. I want to understand what makes a place, a product, or a brand matter to people.
copy.dimension.business.title: Business & growth
copy.dimension.business.copy: I’m interested in the decisions behind the experience: the numbers, the strategy, and the people who turn an idea into something worth building.
copy.dimension.curiosity.title: Curiosity & challenge
copy.dimension.curiosity.copy: New places, unfamiliar projects, and people with a different perspective. I learn the most when I have a reason to step outside what I already know.
copy.home.story: At 15, I started at a local Italian restaurant. I wanted to do more than the job I was given, so I kept asking questions, showing up, and finding ways to learn. Eventually, I earned my place in the kitchen.
copy.home.quote: When something interests me, I want to get closer to it. Understand it. And find a way to be part of it.
copy.home.rbi: My summer at Restaurant Brands International brought my interest in restaurants into a new setting: the business behind brands serving people every day. I joined as an LDP Summer Analyst and will return as an Incoming LDP Analyst.
copy.story.lead: Before the business classes and internships, there was a local Italian restaurant—and a teenager who wanted to know how it all worked.
copy.story.caption: ADD CAPTION: Where was this taken, and what does it mean to you?
copy.story.start: When I was 15, I started working at a local Italian restaurant, helping with cleaning and customer service. What caught my attention wasn’t just the food. It was the pace, the people, and all the small things that had to come together to make a restaurant work.
copy.story.persist: I wanted to learn in the kitchen, but at first I was told I was too young. I kept asking questions, staying longer, and learning whenever I could. Eventually, I earned the chance to cook and take on more responsibility.
copy.story.lesson: That experience changed how I approach opportunities. When I care about something, I want to understand it, get involved, and show through my actions that I can do more.
copy.story.next: At the University of Miami, that same curiosity has led me into business, analytical work, leadership, and projects with teams. My summer at Restaurant Brands International connected those experiences back to the industry where it started.
copy.story.future: I’m interested in where restaurants, consumer brands, and business development meet. I don’t have every next step mapped out. I do know I want to keep working on things that make me curious enough to go further.
copy.experience.rbi: Working in marketing analytics gave me a different view of the restaurant industry: how data can help teams ask better questions about products, menus, and performance.
copy.experience.rbi.learning: A restaurant experience is shaped by decisions customers may never see. I’m interested in how those choices connect back to what people order and enjoy.
copy.experience.miami: I’m a fourth-year student at Miami Herbert, studying business and building a foundation for a career around restaurants, consumer brands, and growth.
copy.experience.miami.learning: The projects that stay with me are the ones where I have to turn an idea into a clear recommendation—and explain why it matters.

copy.experience.restaurant: My first restaurant job grew from cleaning and customer service into cooking and greater responsibility. It gave me a firsthand look at the work behind a good guest experience.
copy.experience.restaurant.learning: Showing up consistently, asking to learn, and earning trust can create opportunities that weren’t there at the start.

copy.projects.intro: A place for work that shows how I think: connecting an idea, the people it’s for, and a plan to make it real.
copy.projects.prove: PROVE IT is a sparkling green tea concept developed for a marketing class project. It explores how a beverage brand could connect a product, a point of view, and a launch experience.
copy.projects.origin: The concept draws on a lesson that started in restaurants: confidence grows through preparation, persistence, and doing the work. This project gave me a way to explore that idea through a consumer brand.

copy.beyond.food: I like discovering a great restaurant. I’m just as interested in why it works: the atmosphere, the menu, the service, and the feeling that makes you want to come back.
